On points of the geometric sites.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Theorem <REF_0001> says that the family of points
of <MATH_0001> given by the geometric points of <MATH_0002>
(Lemma <REF_0002>) is conservative, see
Sites, Definition <REF_0003>.
In particular <MATH_0003> has enough points.
<STRUCT_0003> Suppose <MATH_0004> is a sheaf on the big <ACCENT_0001>tale site
<LOCKED_0001>
of <MATH_0005>. Let <MATH_0006> be an object of the big <ACCENT_0002>tale site of <MATH_0007>,
and let <MATH_0008> be a geometric point of <MATH_0009>. Then we define
<MATH_0010> as the stalk
of the restriction <MATH_0011> of <MATH_0012>
to the small <ACCENT_0003>tale site of <MATH_0013>. In other words, we can define
the stalk of <MATH_0014> at any geometric point of any
scheme <MATH_0015>.
<STRUCT_0004> The big <ACCENT_0004>tale site of <MATH_0016> also has enough points, by
considering all geometric points of all objects of this site, see
(<REF_0004>).
<STRUCT_0005>

<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma should be skipped on a first reading.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0002> be a point of the small <ACCENT_0001>tale site
<MATH_0003> of <MATH_0004> given by a functor
<MATH_0005>.
Then there exists a geometric point <MATH_0006> of <MATH_0007> such that
<MATH_0008> is isomorphic to the point of <MATH_0009> associated to
<MATH_0010> in
Lemma <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0003> Let <MATH_0011> be a point
of the small <ACCENT_0002>tale topos of <MATH_0012>. Then <MATH_0013> comes from a geometric point
of <MATH_0014>, i.e., the stalk functor <MATH_0015>
is isomorphic to a stalk functor as defined in
Definition <REF_0002>.
<STRUCT_0004>
